SREBot: :rotating_light: ALERT: sudden spike in 5xx/timeouts for /v1/generate in us-west-2. error rate ~14% over last 2m, p99 ~7800ms. triggered pager. grafana: https://grafana/redwood/d/abc123/gateway-overview?orgId=1&from=now-5m
Kim (oncall): Ack. I'm on it. Seeing gateway 504/502 across multiples backends, started ~2026-03-15T09:10Z. Any recent deploys?
Mika (runtime): I see canary deploy finished at 09:09:47 UTC — rollout id: rollout/inf-2026-03-15-canary-7. Commit abc123def. Could be multiplexing or changed retry behavior.
Kim (oncall): Good catch. Pulling logs now. Can someone check pod-level latencies for runtime pool-3?
DevOps (deploy-bot): Deploy event: canary rollout inf-service v2 -> v3 (abc123def) completed 09:09:50. no auto-rollback.
Kim (oncall): Logs showing repeated timeouts on gRPC upstream in the canary pods. sample tail:
```
2026-03-15T09:11:12Z runtime-7fdc kube: ERROR upstream call timeout: context deadline exceeded (deadline 5s)
2026-03-15T09:11:12Z runtime-7fdc gateway: 504 /v1/generate uid=aa12  seq_len=512
2026-03-15T09:11:13Z runtime-7fdc cache: evict shard 3 (pressure)
2026-03-15T09:11:14Z runtime-7fdc gpu-kernel: enqueue wait 120ms
```
Mika (runtime): Interesting — evictions + enqueue waits. I'm seeing connection queue growing on the canary pods: inflight > 400, configured max_inflight=256. That will cause head-of-line and timeouts.
Kim (oncall): Do we have a quick mitigation? Suggest rollback the canary to v2 for immediate relief. Also flip route to stable in us-west-2 routing-policy if possible.
Mika (runtime): Agreed. If we can't tune max_inflight quickly, rollback is fastest. Can DevOps action?
DevOps (deploy-bot): Rolling back rollout/inf-2026-03-15-canary-7 -> previous revision (v2) now. Command: `kubectl rollout undo deployment/inf-service --to-revision=42`. Starting...
DevOps (deploy-bot): Rollback in progress: scaling new pods, draining canary pods, reattaching services.
Kim (oncall): Notifying CS and customer impact team. Lina, can you prepare customer-facing blurb for impacted orgs in us-west?
Lina (support): On it. Drafting: "We're investigating elevated timeouts affecting model generation in us-west-2 after a recent deploy. Mitigation in progress (rollback). We'll update within 15 minutes. If you see persistent errors, please DM support with request IDs." Will post to status.redwood once rollback stabilizes.
Mika (runtime): Quick note: the change in v3 introduced a different batching policy + dynamic concurrency that didn't honor our global max_inflight for heavy sequences. That combination caused runtime to accept more inflight streams until the GPU kernel enqueuing lagged. Root cause likely config + code divergence.
Kim (oncall): Thanks. Monitoring now. p95 jumped from 320ms -> 1.4s, p99 -> 7.8s, error rate 5xx 14% -> target <1%.
DevOps (deploy-bot): Rollback completed at 09:14:30 UTC. Services now pointed back to v2. Healthchecks passing for new pods.
SREBot: Update: error rate dropping. us-west-2 5xx now 3.6% (1m), p99 420ms.
Kim (oncall): Seeing steady decline. Re-running synthetic canary against a replay set.
Mika (runtime): Checking KV cache pressure metrics — evictions back to baseline. Enqueue latency median 8ms. Looks like rollback removed the overload.
SREBot: RESOLVED: error rate back to expected range, p99 restored to baseline 110-160ms for the region. Incident resolved at 09:21:40 UTC.
Kim (oncall): Quick postmortem notes while fresh: timeline, root cause hypothesis (batching + concurrency change bypassed global throttle), immediate mitigation (rollback + routing flip), customer comms. I'll start a short incident report doc and assign follow-ups: (1) safe-guard in deploy pipeline to block canary if inflight > configured threshold, (2) add rollout probe for enqueue latency > 200ms, (3) revert batching change until we have tuning.
Lina (support): Posted status.incident update and notified customers in the affected cohort. No major SLA breaches observed yet, but monitoring continues for error spikes.
Jared (oncall): Picking up handoff. Summary: rollback executed, error rates normal, follow-ups assigned to runtime and deploy teams. I'll run another 30m watch and coordinate the postmortem. Ping me for any re-escalation.
Kim (oncall): Thanks @Jared. Closing active pager. Will link the incident doc here when ready. :white_check_mark:"
